Run order planning

Give one item a demand stock cannot cover, run MRP, and read the plan it makes.

Status

Enterprise Planning, Sales

Applies to

Note

TaskWhat you doResultSteps

Before you start

  • A finished item with an Approved BOM and routing, components, and stock data — the qualified training case from Create test items, such as BAM-CHOP-PAIR with components BAM-ROD and BAM-SLEEVE.

Procedure

1Make the item visible to planning

Result
The finished item and every BOM component have planning data.
Screen
Planning➔Order Planning➔Item Order Plan (cprrp0520m000)

Why LN works this way. The planning screens read an item's planning data, and an item that has none is not refused; it is absent, with nothing to explain why. The link is a row for the planning cluster on the item, and MRP plans a BOM component only if the component has planning data of its own, so this task checks every item in the structure, not just the parent.

StepActionYou should see
1.1Open Item Order Plan (cprrp0520m000)The plan selection screen
1.2Search for the finished itemWrite downfinished itemif it appears, planning data exists: go to step 1.6. If it does not, the item is invisible to planning: continue
1.3Open Items (tcibd0501m000) via Master Data➔Items➔Items and drill into the finished itemItem (tcibd0501m100) opens
1.4On the Clusters tab, add a row with the environment's planning clusterWrite downplanning cluster andsite
1.5Save, then reopen Item Order Plan and search againThe item now appears — an empty plan, but a plan
1.6Repeat steps 1.2–1.5 for every component in the BOMWrite downcomponents given plan dataeach appears in its own Item Order Plan
Make the item visible to planning: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
The item is not in the Item Order PlanIt has no planning data — no cluster row, no plan. Steps 1.3–1.5. Not an error state; nothing will tell you

2Create demand

Result
A sales order exists for more than is on hand.
Screen
Sales➔Orders➔Order Intake Workbench (tdsls4601m200)

Why LN works this way. Planning acts on uncovered demand. A sales order for more than is on hand creates a shortfall, and that shortfall is exactly the quantity MRP should propose, which is what makes the run checkable. Planning sees the demand without the order being approved.

StepActionYou should see
2.1In Inventory 360 (whwmd4300m000), read the finished item's on-hand at its warehouseWrite downfinished item on-hand beforethe demand must exceed this
2.2Create a sales order for the finished item. Follow steps 1–11An order exists at Free
2.3Set Ordered Quantity above the on-hand from step 2.1Write downsales order numberordered quantitythe observed run booked 5 ea against 1 on hand
2.4Set Planned Delivery Date no more than a few days outWrite downplanned delivery date
Create demand: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
LN refuses the item on the sales order — "item sales by sales office not present"The item has no row for the order's sales office. Add it on the Sales Offices tab of Item (tcibd0501m100), then close and reopen the order session
A master-data fix appears to have no effectThe session was already open when the data changed. Close it and reopen

3Put the demand inside the horizon

Result
Planning can see the demand.
Screen
Planning➔Master Data➔Items➔Items - Planning (cprpd1100m000)

Why LN works this way. The order horizon decides which demand planning sees at all: demand beyond it is not late or flagged, it does not exist to planning. LN turns the number of days you enter into a date by counting workdays on the calendar of the item's warehouse, so the date it shows is the one to trust.

StepActionYou should see
3.1Open Items - Planning (cprpd1100m000) for the finished item, Horizons tabOrder Horizon as a number of days, with the resulting date beside it
3.2Compare the delivery date with the horizon date. The delivery date is from step 2.4
3.3If it falls beyond, raise the Order Horizon days until it falls insideWrite downorder horizonrecord both the days entered and the date displayed
3.4Save, and reopen Item Order Plan (cprrp0520m000) for the itemThe Horizons block shows the new Order Horizon date
3.5Find the demand in the gridA Sales Order row with your order number and quantity as Demand
Put the demand inside the horizon: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
The demand does not appear in the Item Order PlanThe delivery date is beyond the Order Horizon date. Step 3.2 — and remember the date is not today plus your days

4Run MRP

Result
Planned orders exist covering the shortfall, with pegging relations.

Why LN works this way. The run reads every demand inside the horizon, nets it against stock and existing supply, and generates planned orders for the shortfall, multi-level through the BOM when child items are included. With pegging relations updated it also records which demand each planned order exists to serve, which is what Read the pegging tree reads.

StepActionYou should see
4.1Open Generate Order Planning (Item) (cprrp1220m000) for the finished itemScenario and Plan Item are set
4.2Select Include Child ItemsThe run will also plan the BOM components — multi-level, top-down
4.3Confirm Update Pegging Relations is selected, where the field is openRead the pegging tree depends on it — see the notes
4.4Run the generationThe run completes; exception messages print or store if selected
Run MRP: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
The run plans the parent but not a componentThe component has no planning data of its own. Step 1.6 — MRP skips it silently
The run produces nothing at all, or nothing propagates to the parentCheck which item you launched the generation on. Running it from a component does not traverse upward — re-run from the top-level (finished) item, per step 4.1
A component was given planning data and still does not appearIt may be correctly absent — planning proposes supply only for what stock does not cover. Read the component's own Item Order Plan and its on-hand before assuming the fix failed.

5Review the result

Result
The planned supply is read on both the parent and the component.

Why LN works this way. One planned order plays two roles: it is supply on the parent's plan and demand on the component's, and the component's own plan has already answered it. Planned quantities equal the raw shortfall only when the item's ordering data imposes no lot-size rule; a minimum or a multiple changes the number before you see it.

StepActionYou should see
5.1Reopen the finished item's Item Order PlanThe sales order row now has a companion
5.2Read the planned supply rowWrite downplanned production order number andplanned production quantitya Planned Production Order whose Supply equals ordered quantity minus on-hand
5.3Open the component's Item Order PlanThe same planned production order appears — as Demand
5.4Read the component's planned supply rowWrite downcomponent planned purchase order andcomponent planned quantitya Planned Purchase Order covering what stock does not
5.5Open Planned Orders (cprrp1100m000) for the cluster and site. They are the ones from step 1.4Both planned orders listed, Order Status Planned
Review the result: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
A planned quantity does not equal the raw shortfallOrder-quantity rules in Items - Ordering (tcibd2100m000) round it
An expected planned purchase order is missing entirelyIf the item is a purchase schedule item, supply transfers straight to Purchase Control and no planned purchase order is created — cprrp1100m000 help

6Read the pegging tree

Result
The whole chain reconciles: demand, stock, planned make, planned buy.

Why LN works this way. The pegging tree walks the relations the run recorded: upstream, what will supply this demand; downstream, what demand caused this order. The tree exists only if pegging relations were generated; where the option is locked on, every run generates them.

StepActionYou should see
6.1In Planned Orders, select the planned production order from step 5.5
6.2Run Pegging - UpstreamOrder Pegging (cprrp0740m200) opens as a tree
6.3Read the tree from the topThe sales order, then each level of stock and planned supply beneath it
6.4Check the arithmetic at every level against the BOM and the stock figuresWrite downpegging arithmetic checkeach level's children sum to its requirement
Read the pegging tree: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
The pegging tree is emptyPegging relations were not generated, or the demand lies beyond the Pegging Horizon (cprpd0100m000). See what this task needs before you start

Variations

CaseWhat changes
Run planning for all itemsGenerate Order Planning (cprrp1210m000), Planning➔Order Planning➔Generate Order Planning, runs ranges instead of one item — the production habit. No help is filed for it, so its options are not assumed to match cprrp1220m000's
Net change instead of regenerativeRun a Net Change Planning in the generate session — simulates only from the first net-change date. A value change inside one step, not a different task
Master planningA different mechanism, not a value change: enabling Master Plan on cprpd1100m000 splits the horizons, and the item master plan must be initialized before it exists. Its own process when written — it needs cprpd/cprmp session help first

What comes next

WhenThenStart at
Planned orders cover the shortfall and reconcile in the pegging tree—
The planned quantities look wrong against supplier realityAdjust order-quantity rules in Items - Ordering (tcibd2100m000) and rerun Run MRPRun MRP
